note: The decimal length field from the mangled input is converted into the local int number used as a source-name length.
The input digits 2147483648 are accumulated without an overflow check, so the int length value can wrap outside the valid positive source-name range.
The wrapped parsed length is passed directly to ParseIdentifier as the source-name identifier length.
The only rejected negative length is -1; other negative lengths are not rejected before they are used as an identifier size and cursor offset.
The negative length moves the parser cursor backward before the stack input buffer instead of advancing within the NUL-terminated mangled string.
After the malformed source name is accepted, the optional ABI-tag parser is evaluated using the corrupted cursor.
ParseAbiTag reaches this token check with state->mangled_cur pointing outside the stack buffer, causing a one-byte out-of-bounds read.
